title: Investment Funds Supervision
summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors to oversee investment funds and their managers, from authorisation and valuation to liquidity, leverage, private markets and tokenised funds.
intro: This training programme equips supervisory staff to oversee investment funds and their managers across the fund value chain: assessing authorisation, valuation, liquidity and leverage, challenging costs and delegation, and responding to private, sustainable and tokenised funds.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give supervisors a structured understanding of how investment funds are built, managed, distributed and regulated, and where investor harm and financial stability risk typically arise. Participants leave able to map supervisory risks across the fund value chain, test firms' valuation, liquidity and delegation arrangements, spot red flags early and decide on a proportionate supervisory response.
sections.What It Covers: Fund structures and the value chain, supervisory risks and international standards, authorisation and depositaries, valuation, liquidity risk management and liquidity management tools, leverage and money market funds, disclosure, costs and distribution, delegation and substance, private market funds, and sustainable and tokenised funds.
Intended Audience: Supervisors, inspectors and authorisation staff responsible for fund managers, funds, depositaries and fund administrators
Policy, risk and financial stability specialists working on asset management and non-bank financial intermediation
Team leaders and heads of department setting supervisory priorities for the funds sector
Learning Objectives: Explain how investment funds operate across the value chain and where supervisory risks arise
Apply international standards for collective investment schemes to authorisation and ongoing supervision
Assess valuation, liquidity and leverage risk, including the use of liquidity management tools
Challenge managers on disclosure, costs and charges, distribution and delegation arrangements
Evaluate the risks of private market, sustainable and tokenised funds and the claims made for them
Design a proportionate supervisory response to fund-level and manager-level red flags
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day workshops. Each module combines a technical briefing with case studies, break-out exercises and supervisory question sets, and modules can be selected or tailored to the authority's funds sector.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of supervising or authorising asset managers or funds is helpful. No specialist investment or quantitative background is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Revised Policy Recommendations to Address Structural Vulnerabilities from Liquidity Mismatch in Open-Ended Funds (2023)
IOSCO, Recommendations for Liquidity Risk Management for Collective Investment Schemes (2018)
IOSCO, Principles for the Valuation of Collective Investment Schemes (2013)
IOSCO, Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation (2017)

modules.title: Investment Funds and the Fund Value Chain
modules.summary: Level-setting on what investment funds are, why investors use them and how the value chain runs from product design and distribution through portfolio management to operations and administration.
objectives: Explain how an investment fund operates and its benefits and risks for investors
Describe the roles of managers, depositaries, administrators, distributors and auditors
Map fund regulation onto the value chain using a simple supervisory schema
syllabus: Open-ended, closed-ended, listed and money market fund structures
Retail funds versus alternative funds for professional investors
The value chain: product, distribution, management, operations and administration
Market size, growth and concentration in the domestic funds sector

modules.title: Supervisory Risks and International Fund Standards
modules.summary: The main sources of investor harm and systemic risk in funds and asset management, and how international standards and typical fund regulatory regimes are designed to mitigate them.
objectives: Identify the key supervisory risks in funds and asset management
Explain the IOSCO principles and standard-setter work relevant to collective investment schemes
Distinguish retail fund product rules from regimes for alternative fund managers
syllabus: Risk mapping: conflicts, investment, liquidity, operational and conduct risk
IOSCO Objectives and Principles and the collective investment scheme standards
Product-regulated retail funds versus manager-regulated alternative funds
Workshop: mapping supervisory risk areas to the regulatory schema

modules.title: Fund Authorisation, Product Rules and Depositaries
modules.summary: How the authority assesses fund and manager applications, the product rules that protect retail investors, and the safekeeping and oversight role of the depositary.
objectives: Assess a fund or manager application against authorisation criteria
Explain eligible asset, diversification and concentration rules for retail funds
Evaluate whether the depositary provides effective safekeeping and independent oversight
syllabus: Authorisation of managers and funds: programme of operations, people and resources
Eligible assets, diversification limits and borrowing restrictions
Depositary duties: safekeeping, cash monitoring and oversight of the manager
Red flags in fund applications and depositary arrangements

modules.title: Fund Valuation and Pricing
modules.summary: How funds value their assets and calculate net asset value, why valuation of illiquid and hard-to-value assets demands close scrutiny, and how supervisors test valuation governance.
objectives: Explain valuation and pricing standards for collective investment schemes
Assess valuation governance, independence and conflicts of interest
Identify red flags in valuation of illiquid and hard-to-value assets
syllabus: Net asset value calculation, pricing errors and investor compensation
Valuation policies, committees and the independence of the valuation function
Hard-to-value assets: models, stale prices and manager discretion
Case study: valuation red flags in a fund under stress

modules.title: Liquidity Risk Management and Liquidity Management Tools
modules.summary: How open-ended funds manage the mismatch between dealing frequency and asset liquidity, how stress testing and liquidity management tools work, and what happens when a fund suspends dealing.
objectives: Explain liquidity mismatch and the FSB and IOSCO recommendations on fund liquidity
Assess liquidity stress testing, redemption assumptions and liquidity management tools
Evaluate a manager's handling of a suspension or gating event
syllabus: Liquidity mismatch, first-mover advantage and dilution of remaining investors
Liquidity stress testing: redemption modelling and asset liquidity assumptions
Liquidity management tools: swing pricing, anti-dilution levies, notice periods and gates
Case study: an open-ended fund suspension and lessons for supervisors

modules.title: Leverage, Money Market Funds and Systemic Risk
modules.summary: How funds use borrowing and derivatives to create leverage, how leverage is measured and limited, and why money market funds and leveraged funds matter for financial stability.
objectives: Explain how leverage is created, measured and reported by funds
Assess the use of leverage limits and supervisory data to identify risk
Evaluate money market fund structures, run risk and reform options
syllabus: Gross, commitment and risk-based leverage measures and the IOSCO framework
Derivatives, securities financing and counterparty exposure in funds
Money market funds: constant and variable net asset value models and run dynamics
Using supervisory data to monitor leverage and systemic risk

modules.title: Disclosure, Costs and Charges, and Distribution
modules.summary: What investors must be told before and after they invest, how fund costs are regulated to prevent undue charges, and how funds are marketed and distributed domestically and across borders.
objectives: Assess the quality and consistency of key investor disclosures
Challenge managers on cost transparency, undue costs and value for investors
Explain cross-border fund distribution, recognition and marketing rules
syllabus: Prospectus, key information documents and periodic reporting
Ongoing charges, performance fees, transaction costs and closet indexing
Assessing value for money and the prevention of undue costs
Cross-border distribution, recognition regimes and marketing communications

modules.title: Delegation, Outsourcing and Manager Substance
modules.summary: How fund managers delegate portfolio management, risk management and administration, how supervisors test whether the manager retains real control, and the operational resilience risks delegation creates.
objectives: Explain the regulatory framework for delegation and outsourcing by fund managers
Assess whether a manager retains effective oversight and sufficient substance
Identify concentration, continuity and letter-box entity risks
syllabus: Delegation models: portfolio management, risk management, administration and distribution
Substance tests: people, expertise, decision-making and oversight evidence
Third-party concentration, technology dependency and operational resilience
Red flags of letter-box entities and white-label platforms

modules.title: Private Market Funds and Retailisation
modules.summary: How private equity, private credit and real asset funds are structured, why they need a different supervisory lens, and the investor protection implications of opening private markets to retail investors.
objectives: Explain private equity, private credit and real asset fund structures
Evaluate liquidity and valuation risk in semi-liquid and long-term funds
Assess the investor protection implications of retail access to private markets
syllabus: Closed-ended, evergreen and semi-liquid private market fund structures
Fee structures, alignment of interest and conflicts in private funds
Long-term investment fund regimes and retail access to private markets
Case study: a supervisory risk assessment of a semi-liquid private credit fund

modules.title: Sustainable Funds, Tokenised Funds and the Supervisory Horizon
modules.summary: Brings the programme together by examining sustainability-related fund disclosures and greenwashing, fund tokenisation, and the regulatory topics shaping fund supervision, ending with a supervisory planning workshop.
objectives: Assess sustainability claims, fund labels and disclosures for greenwashing risk
Explain how tokenisation and distributed ledgers change fund operations and risk
Prioritise emerging fund risks in a supervisory plan
syllabus: Sustainability disclosures, fund categorisation and naming rules
Greenwashing and greenbleaching: evidence, red flags and supervisory response
Tokenised fund units: issuance, transfer agency, custody and settlement
Workshop: a twelve-month supervisory plan for the funds sector

related.title: Asset Management and Investment Fund Regulation: International Edition
related.summary: A ten-module programme mapping asset management and fund regulation through IOSCO and FSB standards, from fund regimes and delegation to liquidity, cross-border distribution, sustainability and resilience.

related.title: EU Asset Management and Investment Fund Regulation (EU Edition)
related.summary: A ten-module programme mapping EU fund and asset management regulation, from UCITS, AIFMD and MiFID II to liquidity, delegation, cross-border marketing, SFDR and DORA.

related.title: Fund Regulation Country Briefings
related.summary: Eleven country webinar briefings on fund vehicles, regulators, authorisation, distribution and recent developments in leading European, offshore and Asia Pacific fund markets.

related.title: International Fund Regulation: Global and Regional Briefings
related.summary: A ten-module webinar series mapping international, EU and Asia Pacific fund regulation and how cross-border fund distribution, management and investment are regulated.

related.title: Introduction to Investment Funds: From Launch to Wind-Down
related.summary: A fourteen-module foundation programme taking new funds professionals and supervisors through every stage of an investment fund, from structure and regulation to operations and wind-down.

related.title: Investment Management and Private Markets Supervision
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors to oversee investment, wealth and private market managers, including private credit, leverage, valuation and non-bank systemic risk.
